teaser: Send a QR code and a link to a public key: the workflow the QR experiment opens, who already does this, and a format to share.
core_idea: Publishing a public key as a QR code and a link lets anyone, person or agent, return a secret encrypted to it as another QR code carrying their own key, so one exchange becomes a two-way, serverless channel trusted by a one-time fingerprint check; each piece is proven elsewhere, and the experiment's QRE1 frame can become a shared format with chunking, forward secrecy and an identity.

figures.caption: The workflow: publish my public key as a QR code and a link; their browser or agent encrypts the secret to it and adds its own public key; the ciphertext travels as a QR code by any channel; I decrypt it and check their fingerprint once; from then on it is two-way. Agents do the same.

Who already moves keys and secrets in QR codes: the EU Digital COVID Certificate, key verification in Signal, WhatsApp and Matrix, device linking in Signal and WhatsApp, Threema, passkeys on another device, offline wallets, Keybase and OpenKeychain, and provisioning codes for authenticators, Wi-Fi, WireGuard and eSIMs.

Anatomy of a QRE1 frame: the version, the recipient's key id, the sender's one-off X25519 key, a nonce, the ChaCha20-Poly1305 ciphertext, and optionally the sender's Ed25519 key and signature, in one line of text.
